recent_events.title: QS World University Rankings 2026: AUCA ranked best university in Kyrgyzstan
recent_events.description: In the newly released QS World University Rankings 2026, AUCA achieved 1st place among all universities in Kyrgyzstan, top 13 in Central Asia, ranked within the 901-950 bracket globally, and 193rd worldwide for International Student Diversity (score 81.5). Five Kyrgyz universities entered the global ranking.
recent_events.impact: Marks the second consecutive year AUCA has been recognized as Kyrgyzstan's leading university in the QS global ranking

recent_events.title: Bard College appoints former AUCA President Jonathan Becker as Acting President
recent_events.description: The Bard College Board of Trustees appointed Executive Vice President and Vice President for Academic Affairs Jonathan Becker - former AUCA president (2021-2023) and AUCA trustee - as acting president of Bard College during a comprehensive search for a new permanent leader.
recent_events.impact: Strengthens the AUCA-Bard partnership at the leadership level; Becker remains on AUCA Board of Trustees

recent_events.title: AUCA Commencement Ceremony 2026
recent_events.description: On June 6, AUCA held its Commencement Ceremony celebrating the Class of 2026, bringing together graduates, faculty, staff, families, friends, and distinguished guests.
recent_events.impact: Annual flagship event marking successful completion of studies for the graduating cohort

recent_events.title: Over 3 years of collaboration with Spirit of America to support Afghan students
recent_events.description: AUCA and Spirit of America have collaborated for more than 3 years through the Afghan Future Campaign to support Afghan students studying at AUCA after the 2021 fall of Kabul, providing resources for classroom success and student initiatives.
recent_events.impact: Sustained humanitarian educational support for displaced Afghan students in Central Asia

recent_events.title: Delegation from the National Library of Kazakhstan visits AUCA
recent_events.description: On June 17-19, 2026, AUCA welcomed a delegation from the Conservation, Restoration, and Bookbinding Service of the National Library of the Republic of Kazakhstan, and hosted the annual 'Academic Libraries: Traditions and Innovations' training for university libraries in Kyrgyzstan.
recent_events.impact: Regional knowledge exchange positioning AUCA Library as a Central Asian leader in academic library practices

recent_events.title: AUCA signs MoU with Azizi Group for $500,000 in Afghan student financial aid
recent_events.description: The American University of Central Asia signed a memorandum of understanding with the Azizi Group, a UAE-based real estate and investment company, to provide $500,000 in financial support for AUCA Afghan students whose education was disrupted by the suspension of international funding.
recent_events.impact: Secured alternative funding ensuring continuity of education for vulnerable Afghan students

recent_events.title: Center for Civic Engagement concludes 'Sort It 2.0' eco-quest
recent_events.description: AUCA's Center for Civic Engagement concluded the 'Sort It 2.0' (Сортируй 2.0) eco-quest on April 24, held in two stages (October-November 2025 and February-April 2026) to promote waste sorting and environmental awareness.
recent_events.impact: Reinforces AUCA's role as a leader in environmental sustainability education in Kyrgyzstan

core_business: Private, non-profit liberal arts university offering American-style Bachelor of Arts degrees in 15 undergraduate programs and 10+ graduate programs. First higher education institution in Central Asia operating on the American model with credit-hour system and liberal arts curriculum, providing U.S.-accredited degrees through partnership with Bard College. Also authorized to confer the Kyrgyz National Diploma.
apec_stance: AUCA functions as a U.S.-backed soft-power anchor in Central Asia. Founded with U.S. government and Open Society Institute funding, it is the only university in the region delivering American-accredited liberal arts degrees (via Bard College partnership since 2010). USAID has recognized it as the first higher education institution in Central Asia functioning according to the American model, with credit-hour system, liberal arts curriculum, and commitment to democratic values, freedom of expression and inquiry. The university maintains strong ties with U.S. institutions (Bard College, American Councils, Indiana University historical partnerships), hosts displaced Afghan students, and consistently promotes Western-style democratic transformation of Central Asia. It is a key conduit for U.S. cultural and educational influence in the region.
